evidence.claim: Archrock describes itself as a provider of natural gas compression services to U.S. energy customers and a supplier of aftermarket services to customers that own compression equipment.
Archrock states that compression equipment is used in natural gas production, gathering, processing, storage, and pipeline transmission contexts.
Natural Gas Services Group identifies Rental, Sales, and Aftermarket Services as its operating units and states that it maintains and services the compression equipment it rents to customers.
evidence.source_title: Natural Gas Services Group, Inc. 2024 Form 10-K

evidence.claim: Natural Gas Services Group reported 1,912 natural gas compressors in its rental fleet totaling 598,840 horsepower as of Dec. 31, 2024.
evidence.source_title: Natural Gas Services Group, Inc. 2024 Form 10-K

evidence.claim: MRC Global describes itself as a leading global distributor of pipe, valves and fittings and other infrastructure products and services to diversified gas utility, energy, and industrial end markets.

MRC Global’s 2024 filing says it offers approximately 200,000 SKUs including PVF, valve automation and modification, measurement, instrumentation, and specialty products through a network of more than 7,100 suppliers.
MRC Global disclosed that 96% of its 2024 valve sales were low-emission valves that control methane and other emissions.

memory_update.text: AROC should remain in the oil/gas reliability node as a mid-cap compression and aftermarket supplier; verify whether demand is structurally linked to LNG, transmission, storage, and gas-fired power rather than only upstream activity.

NGS is a small-cap underfollowed compression rental candidate with direct fleet horsepower evidence; keep as a higher-risk discovery-lane name pending utilization, pricing, customer, and large-horsepower mix checks.

MRC is a low-attention PVF/valve/instrumentation distributor candidate; its low-emission valve disclosure creates a methane-compliance angle that should be tested against revenue mix and margin evidence.

For this node, the less obvious investable map is not only LNG exporters or gas producers; it includes compression horsepower, aftermarket service, PVF distribution, low-emission valves, measurement/instrumentation, and project logistics.

Need a follow-up Layer 1C search for public suppliers of gas turbines/reciprocating engines, gensets, emissions monitoring, cryogenic LNG equipment, and methane detection software/hardware; this pass did not fully cover those adjacent chokepoints.

node: Oil/gas reliability, LNG infrastructure, compression, valves, onsite power, and electrification-adjacent equipment
summary: Expanded the node through a two-lane funnel. Reference lane: Cheniere anchors the LNG export and feedgas infrastructure demand chain. Underfollowed lane: Archrock, Natural Gas Services Group, and MRC Global map to less glamorous but potentially chokepoint-relevant functions: natural gas compression services, compressor rental/aftermarket, and pipe-valve-fitting supply-chain distribution for gas utilities, energy, and industrial infrastructure. The strongest direct evidence is for compression and PVF exposure; the market-underappreciation angle remains an inference requiring backlog, utilization, customer mix, and data-center/peaker/LNG project linkage verification.
